releases.notes:
# Against the Wild — 0.0.5 Alpha

The wilderness now has to feed you and keep you through the night. This update adds shelter, food that spoils, ways to preserve it, and three new ways to get food: digging, fishing and trapping.

## 🏕️ Shelter

*   **New: Lean-to.** Build it in place with sticks (Shift + right-click the ground), 2 Primitive Rope and 12 Leafy Branches.
*   Sleeping in a lean-to needs a **lit fire pit within 4 blocks**. The fire burns down to embers overnight.
*   You wake up with a short Regeneration and a little hungry, instead of fully healed.
*   Rain and time wear the covering. Patch it with fresh branches.
*   **Bed recipes are disabled** for now. Beds found in villages still work.
*   **New: Leafy Branch.** Hold right-click on leaves with a knife to cut 2–3, or get one sometimes from breaking leaves by hand. It also works as quick, smoky fire fuel.

## 🍖 Food Spoilage

*   Raw and cooked meat, fish, roots and grubs now **spoil over time**: Fresh → Stale → Spoiling → Rotten.
*   Times follow real life: raw fish lasts 1 day, raw beef 2 days, cooked meat 3 days.
*   Heat speeds spoilage up. Cold biomes, caves and ice slow it down, and food freezes in the snow.
*   Stale and spoiling food is less filling and can give you food poisoning.
*   Cooking does not reset freshness.

## 🌬️ Drying and Smoking

*   **New: Drying Rack** (4 Sticks + 2 Primitive Rope).
*   Dry meat and fish in the sun (about 2 sunny days), or smoke them over a fire pit (8–16 hours).
*   **New: Jerky and Dried Fish.** They keep for 60 days.

## ⛏️ Digging

*   Digging soil by hand is now **very slow** and makes you hungry.
*   **New: Primitive Spade** (knapped stone head) and **Bone Spade**.
*   **The vanilla wooden shovel is disabled.**
*   Dug sod can contain **Wild Roots**, **Wild Onions**, **Grubs**, stones and bones, depending on the biome.
*   An area runs out of finds after a while and recovers over the following days.

## 🐟 Fishing

*   **The spear works underwater:** throw it at fish 2–3 blocks away.
*   A fish the spear kills stays impaled on it, and the spear floats to the surface.
*   **New: Fish Trap** (4 Sticks + 2 Primitive Rope). Set it in water with Grubs or Rotten Flesh as bait. It also catches fish in lakes and ponds.

## 🪢 Snares

*   **New: Snare** (1 Primitive Rope + 2 Sticks). It catches rabbits and chickens while you are away.
*   Bait chooses the prey: roots, onions or carrots for rabbits, seeds for chickens.
*   It works best at dawn and dusk, near bushes, and away from your camp and its smoke.
*   Animals avoid you, so a snare catches nothing while you stand within 8 blocks.
*   Collect your catch in time. After about 12 hours, **a fox may run off with it** or a wolf may tear the snare apart.
*   No menu: right-click takes the catch straight into your inventory.

## ⚙️ Other

*   New server config sections for spoilage, digging, fishing and snares.

releases.notes:
# Against The Wild — v0.0.4 Alpha

## New Features

### Primitive Flint Axe

- Added a new primitive tool for chopping wood.
- The axe head must first be knapped from flint.
- The finished head is attached to a wooden handle using Primitive Rope.
- Features low durability and realistically slow woodcutting.

### Bark and Tinder Gathering

- The Primitive Knife can now remove bark from birch logs.
- Bark harvesting requires holding the knife against the log for several seconds.
- Harvested trees are visually damaged by becoming stripped.
- Bark harvesting includes working animations, sounds, and particles.
- Birch Bark and dry Plant Fiber can be converted into Tinder Bundles.
- Only a small amount of bark is obtained from each log.

### Primitive Fire Drill

- Added a realistic alternative to early-game flint and steel.
- Crafted using wooden components and Primitive Rope.
- Requires prepared tinder to start a fire.
- Ignition takes several seconds of continuous work.
- The process includes animation, sounds, particles, and progress feedback.
- Rain and wet conditions make ignition significantly more difficult.
- Failed attempts consume the prepared tinder.

### World-Built Fire Pit

- Fire pits are constructed directly in the world.
- Stones, kindling, fuel logs, and tinder are added in separate visual stages.
- Every added stick and log appears individually in the model.
- Prepared fire pits are ignited directly with the Primitive Fire Drill.
- Fires require fuel and burn for a limited amount of time.
- Logs, planks, coal, and charcoal can be used as fuel.
- Uncovered fires are gradually extinguished by rain.
- Water buckets can extinguish fires immediately.
- Burning fire pits melt nearby snow.
- Extinguished fires leave hot embers before turning into ash.
- Embers can be revived using additional sticks and fuel.

#### Cooking Rack

- A cooking rack can be constructed on a burning fire pit.
- The first stick places the two supports.
- The second stick adds the horizontal cooking spit.
- Up to four food items can be placed on the spit.
- Food cooks more slowly than on a standard Minecraft campfire.
- Cooking food is displayed directly on the rack.

### Stone Hammer

- Added the Stone Hammer as the first primitive mining tool.
- Crafted from a large Rock, a Stick, and either Plant Fiber, Primitive Rope, or String.
- Has 64 durability and a slow, heavy attack.
- Can collect basic stone materials but cannot recover ores.
- Supported rocks include:

  - Stone
  - Cobblestone
  - Mossy Cobblestone
  - Granite
  - Diorite
  - Andesite
  - Tuff
  - Calcite

- Broken stone produces 2–4 Small Rocks.
- There is a 25% chance to additionally obtain a large Rock.
- Ores are mined extremely slowly and yield no metal.
- Harder materials consume more durability.
- When the hammer breaks, its wooden handle is returned.
- It can be repaired using rocks or binding materials.

releases.notes:
- **Ground clutter system** — sticks, small rocks and rocks now spawn naturally on freshly generated chunks
- **Biome-aware spawning** — rocks and pebbles spawn more frequently near water sources and on underwater floors (riverbeds, lakebeds)
- **Chunk-based generation** — items spawn only once per chunk, on first exploration. No repeated spawning
- **Persistent ground entities** — ground items save and load with the world. They don't disappear on relog
- **Block support logic** — ground items drop as pickable items when the block beneath them is broken
- **Right-click pickup** — pick up any ground item by simply right-clicking it
- **Bare hands wood protection** — breaking any wooden block without a tool is now blocked entirely. No drops, no progress
- **All wood types covered** — protection applies to Oak, Spruce, Birch, Jungle, Acacia, Dark Oak, Mangrove, Cherry, Bamboo, Crimson and Warped wood and all their variants (planks, slabs, fences, doors, signs, etc.)
- **Rock and Small Rock items** — two new custom items added to the game, available in the Against the Wild creative tab
